# A bill owing 100.00 applying a 60.00 split, where a second supplier's
# 200.00 sits on the same expense account.
#
# An ordinary part payment: the director paid 60.00 of this bill and 40.00 is
# still owed. The 200.00 is the other supplier's and stays where it is until
# that bill applies it.
#
# The payment applies a split on the expense account, so it has said which
# split there is this bill's. What is left over is either the other
# supplier's or an unpaid remainder, and accounts alone cannot tell those
# apart.
#
# What this fixture produces: the bill part paid, owing 40.00, with the
# 200.00 split untouched.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
bill "BILL-PART-001"
  vendor_id: "V-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-03-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-03-05
    description: "Supplies"
    account: "Expenses:Supplies:USD"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-03-05
    due: 2026-04-05
    ap_account: "Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD"
    memo: "Bill BILL-PART-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-05
    amount: 60
    account: "Assets:Due From Director USD"
    txn_guid: "7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3"
    txn_split_guid: "8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c37a"
